diagnostic_evidence.quote: and then on the discretised problem using the edge element method.
Secondly, we aim at showing scalability for discretised Maxwell's equation in a waveguide and decomposition into many subdomains when using different types of transmission conditions.

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract, introduction and the opening of Section 4 promise two kinds of numerical results, the second being scalability tests on the edge-element discretised Maxwell problem. Section 4 contains only subsection 4.1. It plots the spectral radius of the modal iteration matrices I^T(r) against their own N→∞ limit. This only checks the finite-N versus limiting-spectrum statement for the continuous, mode-by-mode model. No Schwarz iteration on a discretised Maxwell problem is run, and no measured convergence is compared with the prediction. The claim that experiments confirm prediction of 'practical behavior' is therefore unsupported.

failure_location.quote: Numerical experiments confirm that the limiting spectrum effectively predicts practical behavior even with a modest number of subdomains.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either add the discretised edge-element experiments (actual Schwarz/GMRES iteration counts versus N compared with the limiting-spectrum prediction), or remove or weaken the abstract, introduction and Section 4 statements so they claim only a modal-level illustration.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed validation of the theory on practical discretised waveguide problems, with PEC walls, edge elements and many subdomains, is missing. Only the modal consistency check is supported.
issues.title: Promised discretised (edge-element) experiments and 'practical behavior' confirmation are not delivered
issues.why_classification: The theory is untouched, but a stated experimental contribution must be added or withdrawn. Withdrawing it loses a promised validation without invalidating the formal results.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Now, for a fixed frequency $k=10$, $L= 1$ and overlap $\delta = 0.1$
Furthermore, we demonstrate that the one-level Schwarz method can achieve robustness with respect to the wave number under specific domain decomposition parameters

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract and the fourth listed contribution assert that the paper shows or demonstrates k-robustness for suitable choices of L, δ, ℓ, σ. No theorem, proposition or scaling argument studies the dependence of the limiting factor max(|a+b|,|a−b|) on k. The only experiments use fixed k=10 and k=10+i with fixed L=1 and δ=0.1. Nothing varies k or scales the decomposition parameters with k, so the claim is unsupported by the source.

failure_location.quote: We will also show that, under specific domain decomposition parameters, in addition to scalability, the one-level Schwarz method can also achieve robustness with respect of the wavenumber.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete or weaken the robustness statements in the abstract and contributions. Alternatively, add a supported analysis or experiments in which k varies with suitably scaled L, δ, ℓ, σ and the limiting convergence factor is shown bounded by a constant below 1.
issues.overall_effect: One of the four advertised contributions, k-robustness of the one-level method, has no supporting analysis or evidence. The scalability analysis in N is unaffected.
issues.title: Claimed wavenumber robustness is neither analysed nor demonstrated
issues.why_classification: The least resolution withdraws a headline claim, which is a real loss. The remaining modal analysis and the scalability results stay intact, so the paper remains recognizably comparable.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $\lambda_i^{\rm TE} = -\beta^{\rm TE}_i$, $\lambda^{\rm TM}_i = -\frac{k^2}{\beta^{\rm TM}_i}$ and $\lambda^{\rm TEM}_i = -\imath k$
with $\kappa = \imath \beta^{\rm TE}$ for TE-modes, $\imath k$ for TEM-modes

issues.failure_explanation: By the paper's own eq:lambdaPML, as ℓ→∞ the exponentials vanish and λ^TE→−iβ, λ^TM→−ik²/β, λ^TEM→−ik. With κ=iβ, ik²/β, ik respectively, this gives λ=−κ, not λ=κ. The proof states a third set of values (−β, −k²/β, −ik) that contradicts both the proposition and eq:lambdaPML. Substituting λ=−κ into the formulas for a and b gives a=0 but b=e^{+iβ(L+δ)}. The stated b=e^{−iβ(L+δ)} corresponds to λ=+κ, which is the wrong-direction (absorbing incoming rather than outgoing waves) condition. The two values differ in modulus for evanescent modes: the correct |b| is e^{−|Im β|(L+δ)}, the stated one is e^{+|Im β|(L+δ)}. The conclusion a=0, and hence [I^T]^N=0, survives because it uses only a=0.

failure_location.quote: we have $\lambda^{\rm T}_i = \kappa$ and therefore $a^{\rm T}_i = 0$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State λ^T_i=−κ, recompute b=e^{+iβ(L+δ)} (with Im β≥0 convention), and fix the values of λ in the proof. The nilpotency argument stays unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit transparent-limit values of λ and b are wrong. For evanescent modes the stated b would imply exponential growth. The nilpotency conclusion is unaffected.
issues.title: Transparent (infinite PML) limit: wrong sign of λ (λ=κ instead of −κ) and wrong value of b
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local sign and formula correction using formulas already in the paper, and the nilpotency claim and its proof are preserved.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: (with convention $e^{-\imath \omega t}$ where $\omega$ is the pulsation)

issues.failure_explanation: With time dependence e^{−iωt}, outgoing waves are e^{ikx}, and damping requires Im k>0, i.e. Im ε>0. The paper's ε=ε'−iε'' with ε''>0 gives Im k²<0 (Im k<0), which corresponds to gain, not absorption. The experiment uses k=10+i, where k²=99+20i has positive imaginary part. This corresponds to ε''<0 in the paper's notation, so the stated correspondence between the example and the physical absorptive medium is inconsistent.

failure_location.quote: which corresponds to the case of the complex electric permittivity $\varepsilon = \varepsilon' - \imath \varepsilon''$ with $\varepsilon'' > 0$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use ε=ε'+iε'' with ε''>0 under the e^{−iωt} convention, or switch to the e^{+iωt} convention consistently, including the PML stretching and the definition of outgoing waves.
issues.overall_effect: The physical interpretation of the complex-k experiment, and the claim that it models an absorptive medium, is internally inconsistent. The mathematical content of the plots for k=10+i is unaffected.
issues.title: Sign of the permittivity imaginary part contradicts e^{-iωt} convention and the damped example k=10+i
issues.why_classification: A local sign or convention fix removes the contradiction. No theorem or numerical result changes.
